title: Trellis course manifest
description: Structural schema for a course package's manifest.yaml. Semantic rules that a JSON Schema cannot express (id uniqueness, exactly-one-correct quiz option, sandbox references, path safety, ...) are enforced in code — see validate.ts.

id.description: Stable course id, used as the registry key and in progress records.

Stable module id — also used as a progress key (task 007) and appears unescaped in URLs (GET /courses/:courseId), so it's restricted to URL/id-safe characters (unlike quizOption.id/sandbox.id, which never appear in a URL path).

Stable lesson id — a progress key (task 007) AND a URL path segment (GET /courses/:courseId/lessons/:lessonId), so it's restricted to URL/id-safe characters — no "/", whitespace, or a bare "."/".." (see module.id's doc comment for the same rule).

practice.description: A practice assignment. `type` selects the mechanic: `sql` (the default when absent) runs the learner's SQL in a course sandbox and grades it with `check` (database state -> one boolean), `expected` (the learner's result set vs a reference query's) and/or `solution` (the state the learner's SQL leaves vs the state the author's own solution leaves); `answer` asks the learner to type in the results they got elsewhere (Excel, a BI dashboard) and compares them field by field with `fields[].expected`. WHICH properties are legal depends on `type` — that rule lives in validate.ts, not here, so a course author gets one named error instead of a wall of oneOf branch failures.

type.description: Absent means `sql` — courses written before the second mechanic existed stay valid unchanged.

expected.description: type: sql only. Reference SQL query. The core runs it under the sandbox role in a read-only transaction and compares its result set with the learner's. Never sent to the client.

ordered.description: type: sql only. Does row ORDER matter when comparing against `expected`? Defaults to false (multiset comparison). Only allowed together with `expected` — see dependentRequired above.

solution.description: type: sql only. The author's own SQL solution to the exercise. The core runs it on the freshly seeded sandbox, runs the learner's SQL on an identical one, and compares the resulting database STATES. The strict mechanic for exercises that CHANGE data: it also catches damage the assignment never mentioned (an UPDATE without WHERE). Must be deterministic — no now()/random(), and no seed column whose DEFAULT varies per run. Never sent to the client.

fields.description: type: answer only. The values the learner is asked to report, in the order they are shown.

id.description: Stable field id — the key the client submits its answer under. Unique within the assignment (checked in validate.ts). Same id-safe character set as module/lesson ids.

expected.description: The right answer. Which of the two types is correct depends on the sibling `kind`, so that agreement (and the non-blank rule for text) is checked in validate.ts, where the mismatch can be named instead of reported as "matched no branch". Never sent to the client.

tolerance.description: kind: number only. Absolute tolerance; 0 (the default) means exact equality.
